decisionMemo.businessProblem: A retailer keeps stocking out of best-sellers while cash is trapped in slow movers; the owner suspects forecasting, not demand.

rootCauseDiagnosis.description: Inventory / forecasting mismatch: stock misallocated against demand (stockouts + overstock)
rootCauseDiagnosis.mechanismDescription: Forecast error misallocates stock — stockouts on fast lines alongside overstock on slow lines — trapping cash and forcing markdowns; the issue is planning, not demand or cost.
alternativeExplanations: A one-off supplier disruption rather than a forecasting problem
A deliberate stock build rather than a forecast error

intervention.title: Run a forecast-accuracy and ABC inventory analysis with a demand-segmentation review
intervention.objective: Locate the forecast/stock mismatch before any blanket inventory change
intervention.rationale: A forecast-accuracy and ABC inventory analysis is analysis-only and reversible, sizing forecast error and stock misallocation by SKU class before any replenishment change.
intervention.whyThisNow: Stock is misallocated against demand; the forecast mismatch must be measured before any inventory move

steps.title: Run a forecast-accuracy / ABC inventory analysis
steps.description: Measure forecast error by SKU/ABC class and quantify stockouts vs overstock.
steps.successCriteria: Forecast error and stock misallocation quantified by SKU class

steps.title: Run a demand-segmentation review
steps.description: Segment demand variability to right-size stock by velocity — protecting best-sellers, trimming slow lines.
steps.successCriteria: Velocity-segmented stock plan drafted protecting best-sellers

failureRisks: SKU-level demand history may be sparse for new lines
intervention.fallbackPlan: Apply velocity-segmented adjustments to the worst SKUs first before a broader change

recommendedInterventions.sequencingReason: Quick implementation builds momentum and shows progress

scenarios.name: Aggressive Recovery (Best Case)
scenarios.description: Execute all interventions in optimal sequence with full team commitment
assumptions: Team capacity fully available (no other initiatives)
Client budget approved for all recommended interventions
No external market shocks during implementation
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Revenue recovery within 90 days, competitive positioning restored
risks: Cascading failures if one intervention stumbles

scenarios.name: Staged Implementation (Recommended)
scenarios.description: Execute top 3 prioritized interventions sequentially, measure, then decide on next wave
assumptions: Top 3 interventions address critical path to revenue recovery
Team capacity for 1-2 major initiatives at a time
Monthly review gates to assess progress and adjust
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Measurable improvement in 60 days, foundation for growth set
risks: Slower overall recovery than aggressive path
Competitors may advance while we execute gradually
